text: I felt enormous guilt about missing my grandmother's death. For months I had intrusive images of her face in the black lake. At the funeral I felt like an impostor. I couldn't go near lakes. I became depressed and withdrew from the two friends who had been there, because seeing them reminded me of that night. My mother and I never talked about it, which made it worse.

Seitdem habe ich große Angst vor Straßenbahnen und im Straßenverkehr allgemein. Ich bin ein Jahr lang nicht Fahrrad gefahren. Das Klingeln einer Straßenbahn löst bei mir sofort Herzrasen aus. Am Anfang hatte ich auch Albträume, in denen ich unter der Bahn liege.

The months after the circle were a different kind of darkness from the grief I'd had before. I had pneumonia from the exposure, which took weeks to recover from. But the worst was in my mind.

I had a recurring image of my son at the edge of the slope, his broken face, beckoning. It came at night mostly, but also in the daytime. Sometimes I'd be at the kitchen sink and suddenly feel the cold stones under my body. I felt drawn towards death in a way I hadn't before. Not actively suicidal, but a pull, like the feeling on the mountain that it would be right to go with him. That frightened me and my husband very much.

My grief, which had been heavy but at least clear, became tangled with confusion. Had I really been with my son? Had he wanted me to die? Was it the drug? I couldn't tell anymore what was real.

I felt deep shame about what I had done, and also anger at the facilitators, who I felt had nearly let me die and then called it a gift. I stopped going to yoga because I couldn't face the woman who had recommended it.

I became more depressed than I had ever been. I barely left the house for six months.

For about a year I had HPPD-type symptoms: visual snow, trails, and a slight shimmering on surfaces. I also had bad insomnia for months, I'd lie in bed with that buzzing feeling and couldn't fall asleep, and I'd panic that it was the drug still in my system. I became very anxious about anything that affected my sleep. I lost weight. My girlfriend was supportive but I was on edge all the time. The visuals are milder now but still there.
Ich gehe seitdem nicht mehr in Seen schwimmen.
Derealisation for about four months. My apartment and the world often looked 'rendered', and I'd get panicky if things seemed to lag. I gave up VR completely and played much less in general.
I stopped the ketamine treatment. I had panic attacks for a few weeks, especially at night when I was alone. My depression went back to where it was before.

Nach dieser Nacht hatte ich lange Zeit große Angst vor der Polizei. Wenn ich ein Polizeiauto gesehen habe, bekam ich Herzrasen und musste die Straßenseite wechseln. Ich hatte Albträume von Uniformen mit glühenden Augen und von grellem Licht. Ich konnte eine Zeit lang nicht schlafen, wenn im Haus jemand geklingelt hat. Dazu kam die Angst vor dem Strafverfahren, das monatelang offen war, bevor es eingestellt wurde. Ich habe mich in dieser Zeit sehr zurückgezogen und war depressiv. Ich habe mich auch von der spirituellen Szene, in der ich mich bewegt hatte, abgewandt, weil ich mich verraten gefühlt habe.
Headaches for a while. Nothing else really.

For a long time after the retreat I couldn't be in the dark. I slept with all the lights on, and I bought a small light for the bathroom so I'd never have to be in darkness, even for a second. Power cuts were terrifying. When I closed my eyes I sometimes saw the eyes on the walls opening.

I had the persistent sense of a presence near me, especially at night. I'd feel something sitting on the edge of the bed. I knew it wasn't real but I felt it. This went on for about eight months.

I had episodes of depersonalisation, mostly when it got dark in the evening, where I'd feel like I was dissolving back into that black space and that my life was the dream. During these episodes I'd have to grab something solid and say my name out loud.

Panic attacks came in small rooms and corridors with corners, like hotel corridors, basements, elevators. I'd feel like the walls were endless and I'd never find the way out.

I was depressed and also very angry, at myself, but mainly at the organiser who didn't come when I knocked and then made me wait another hour. I felt that he had treated my terror as a 'process' when I needed help.

My concentration was bad. I made mistakes at work. My partner said I seemed far away all the time.

It's been almost two years now. Most of it has eased, but I still sleep with a night light and I still can't stand total darkness.

Ich habe danach monatelang Spiegel gemieden und mich hässlich gefühlt. Das hat sich auf mein Selbstwertgefühl ausgewirkt. Ich hatte auch Angst, dass mein Gesicht wieder anfängt zu schmelzen, und habe mich ständig kontrolliert.
Some sad and shaky weeks. But mostly I feel the session finally let me feel what I'd been carrying since childhood. I'm more connected to my mother now.
